cases.sentence: То невраждебное, но холодное ___ опять установилось между братьями.
cases.translation: That not-unfriendly but cold relation was again established between the brothers.
cases.explain: Отношение is the subject of установилось (was established), so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Не доезжая с четверть версты от ___, Левин увидал бегущих ему навстречу детей.
cases.translation: Not yet a quarter of a mile from the house, Levin saw the children running to meet him.
cases.explain: The preposition от (from) governs the genitive case.

cases.sentence: Дойдя по узкой ___ до нескошенной полянки, Левин поместил своих гостей в тени осинок.
cases.translation: Walking along the narrow path to the unmown glade, Levin seated his guests in the shade of the young aspens.
cases.explain: The preposition по (along) governs the dative case.

cases.sentence: Левин сел в ___ и взял вожжи.
cases.translation: Levin got into the trap and took the reins.
cases.explain: The preposition в (into) with a verb of motion governs the accusative case here.

cases.sentence: Кучер, подъехав к стаду, поговорил что-то с ___.
cases.translation: The coachman, having ridden up to the herd, said something to the herdsman.
cases.explain: The preposition с (with) governs the instrumental case.

cases.sentence: Левин поместил своих гостей в тени осинок на ___.
cases.translation: Levin seated his guests in the shade of the young aspens on a bench.
cases.explain: The preposition на (on) governs the prepositional case here, denoting location.

reading.ru: Левин смотрел перед собой и видел стадо.
reading.question: What did Levin see in front of him as he sat lost in thought?
reading.explain: The text says Levin looked ahead of him and saw a herd.

reading.ru: Потом увидал свою тележку, запряженную вороным, и кучера, который, подъехав к стаду, поговорил что-то с пастухом.
reading.question: What did Levin notice next, after the herd?
options: His own trap harnessed to a black horse, and the coachman speaking with the herdsman
reading.correct: His own trap harnessed to a black horse, and the coachman speaking with the herdsman
reading.explain: He then saw his own trap harnessed to a black horse and the coachman talking with the herdsman.

reading.ru: Левин сел в тележку и взял вожжи.
reading.question: What did Levin do when he came to his senses?
options: He got into the trap and took the reins
He began arguing with the coachman
reading.correct: He got into the trap and took the reins
reading.explain: The text says Levin got into the trap and took the reins.

reading.ru: «Пожалуйста, не трогай и не учи меня», — сказал Левин, раздосадованный этим вмешательством Кучера.
reading.question: How did Levin respond when the coachman corrected his driving?
options: He told him not to touch or teach him, feeling annoyed
reading.correct: He told him not to touch or teach him, feeling annoyed
reading.explain: Annoyed by the coachman's interference, Levin told him not to touch or instruct him.

reading.ru: Не доезжая с четверть версты от дома, Левин увидал бегущих ему навстречу Гришу и Таню.
reading.question: Who came running to meet Levin as he neared home?
reading.explain: Not yet a quarter mile from home, Levin saw Grisha and Tanya running to meet him.

reading.ru: Только загнув за поворот дороги и увидав шедших навстречу, Левин узнал Котовасова в соломенной шляпе, шедшего точно так, размахивая руками, как представляла Таня.
reading.question: Who did Levin recognize walking toward him in a straw hat?
reading.explain: Rounding the bend, Levin recognized Katavasov in a straw hat, walking exactly as Tanya had imitated.

reading.ru: Котовасов очень любил говорить о философии, имея о ней понятие от естественников, никогда не занимавшихся философией.
reading.question: What was Katavasov's attitude toward philosophy?
options: He loved discussing it, though his understanding came from natural scientists who had never studied philosophy
He refused to discuss it with Levin
reading.correct: He loved discussing it, though his understanding came from natural scientists who had never studied philosophy
reading.explain: The text says Katavasov loved talking about philosophy, though his ideas about it came from natural scientists who never actually studied it.

reading.ru: Выйдя из тележки и поздоровавшись с братом и Котовасовым, Левин спросил про жену.
reading.question: What did Levin do right after getting out of the trap and greeting his brother and Katavasov?
options: He went straight to the beehives
reading.explain: After getting out and greeting them, Levin asked about his wife.

reading.ru: Она перенесла Митю в колок — это был лес около дома.
reading.question: Where had Kitty taken their son Mitya?
options: Into a small wood (колок) near the house
reading.correct: Into a small wood (колок) near the house
reading.explain: The text explains she had carried Mitya into the колок, a small wood near the house.

reading.ru: Левин всегда отсоветовал жене носить ребенка в лес, находя это опасным, и известие это было ему неприятно.
reading.question: How did Levin feel about his wife carrying the baby into the woods?
options: He was displeased, having always advised against it as dangerous
He was delighted by the idea
reading.correct: He was displeased, having always advised against it as dangerous
reading.explain: Levin had always advised his wife against it, finding it dangerous, and the news displeased him.

reading.ru: «Ну, что ты делаешь?» — сказал Сергей Иванович, отставая от других и равняясь с братом.
reading.question: What did Sergei Ivanovich ask Levin as they walked together?
options: Whether he had read his book
reading.explain: Falling behind the others to walk alongside his brother, Sergei Ivanovich asked, "Well, what are you doing?"

reading.ru: «Недельки на две. Очень много дела в Москве».
reading.question: How long did Levin say he would be staying?
reading.explain: Levin answered that he would stay for about two weeks, since there was much business in Moscow.

reading.ru: Сергей Иванович улыбнулся на умышленность вопроса.
reading.question: How did Sergei Ivanovich react to Levin's pointed question about reviews of his book?
options: He smiled at the deliberateness of the question
reading.correct: He smiled at the deliberateness of the question
reading.explain: Sergei Ivanovich smiled at how deliberate (pointed) the question was.

reading.ru: И довольно было этих слов, чтобы то невраждебное, но холодное отношение друг к другу, которого Левин так хотел избежать, опять установилось между братьями.
reading.question: What kind of relationship persisted between the two brothers despite Levin's wish to avoid it?
options: A cool, though not hostile, mutual reserve
reading.correct: A cool, though not hostile, mutual reserve
reading.explain: Those few words were enough to re-establish the not-unfriendly but cold relation Levin had wanted to avoid.

reading.ru: «Как хорошо вы сделали, что вздумали приехать», — сказал он ему.
reading.question: What did Levin say to Katavasov about his visit?
options: That it was good of him to think of coming
That he should not have come
That he was too busy to talk
reading.correct: That it was good of him to think of coming
reading.explain: Levin told Katavasov it was good that he had decided to come.

reading.ru: У самых синей одна пчела завизжала, запутавшись ему в бороду, но он осторожно выпростил ее.
reading.question: What happened to Levin near the beehives?
options: A bee got tangled in his beard, buzzing, but he carefully freed it
He was chased away by bees
reading.correct: A bee got tangled in his beard, buzzing, but he carefully freed it
reading.explain: A bee got tangled in his beard and buzzed, but he carefully freed it.

reading.ru: Он вспомнил, что уже успел рассердиться на Ивана, выказать холодность брату и легкомысленно поговорить с Котовасовым.
reading.question: What did Levin recall about his own behavior that day?
options: That he had gotten angry at Ivan, been cold to his brother, and spoken carelessly with Katavasov
That he had been perfectly calm all day
That he had forgotten to feed the bees
That he had lost his hat
reading.correct: That he had gotten angry at Ivan, been cold to his brother, and spoken carelessly with Katavasov
reading.explain: He remembered that he had already managed to get angry at Ivan, show coldness to his brother, and speak flippantly with Katavasov.
